review.brief:
Review change RM57-charging-verifysession-takes-ref (module charging, roadmap RM57 tier 3). Read the diff of commits 2d308b7, d7f7860, 06fd52a - not the whole module.

WHAT IT DOES: charging.SessionVerifier.VerifySession's second parameter changes from teslaID int64 to ref vehicleref.Ref. The implementation unwraps ref.TeslaID() on its first line. No SQL, schema, migration or sqlc change.

VALIDATE:
1. Module boundary. internal/charging now imports internal/vehicleref. Confirm this creates no cycle and breaks no rule in ai/architecture.md. vehicleref imports nothing project-local by design.
2. The three read ports - ListSessionsByVehicleBetween, ListSessionsByVehicleUpdatedSince, ListSessionsByVehicle - MUST still take teslaID int64. internal/analytics calls all three and cannot legally build a Ref. Retyping any of them is a blocker finding.
3. Test contract. design.md D6 says NO test's expected value changes, only its call syntax. Verify the 30 substitutions across the 5 charging test files changed only the one argument - no assertion, fixture or expected value. This is the anti-gaming check that matters most here.
4. No vehicleref:allow marker anywhere in internal/charging. The guard now exempts _test.go files, so none is needed. A marker means someone worked around the guard instead of using the exemption.
5. Doc comments. The two VerifySession comments were rewritten to remove 19 pointers into archived design docs. Check the reasons that replaced them are ACCURATE against the archived designs (RM31 verification port, RM41 session status, the derived start-battery-pct change) and that no behavioural detail was lost. An invented reason is a blocker; a lost detail is a finding.
6. Docs track change: internal/charging/AGENTS.md Allowed Imports, and the two KB guides whose printed signature changed.
7. Spec coverage: specs/charging/spec.md's MODIFIED requirement matches what shipped.

EXPECTED AND NOT A FINDING: go build ./... is RED at internal/gateway/handlers/supercharger.go:681. That call site belongs to tier 4 (RM57-gateway-authorize-supercharger-reads) and is deliberately left broken. Do not raise it, and do not fix it.

SIGNALS - who ran what: the assistant ran go build, go vet, gofmt -l, vehicleref-guard, boundary-guard, archive-guard and openspec validate --strict, all clean. The leader re-ran every one independently. The TEST SUITE was run by the OWNER, not the assistant - judge test quality by READING the tests, never by running them.

TEST-EXECUTION-POLICY (verbatim): Claude writes tests but never runs the suite - never go test ./..., make test, make test-with-db or make check. It MAY run go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build, make vet, make bins, and the standalone guards. The owner runs the suite and reports results; work that is complete but unexecuted is awaiting-user-verification, never done, and a passing suite is recorded as the owner's report, never claimed by the assistant.

B2 WRITING RULE (verbatim, binds every word you write): Short sentences - one idea each, 15 words or fewer. Common words only: no idioms, no phrasal verbs, no rare vocabulary - write 'use' not 'leverage', 'start' not 'kick off', 'problem' not 'caveat'. Keep technical terms in English and never rename or simplify an identifier, but explain the result in simple words. No filler. Code comments say WHY and must never cite design.md, a decision ID, a change ID, a roadmap ID or a tier number.

PERFORMANCE-PROFILE (verbatim): read-heavy - read performance is mandatory over write performance; writes are mostly done by pollers at midnight, so denormalizing, indexing aggressively, and precomputing for reads is acceptable - never at the cost of the modular-monolith boundaries or module data ownership.
